scope: Read-only local source and zero-filesystem-extraction transport inspection; no installer, CI, compiler, binder, archive program or host request executed.
reviewed_properties: Installer requires normal assertion-enabled Python, Linux uid1000 and an owned non-group/world-writable fixed qualified ROOT.
The transport archive is pinned by exact35344 bytes and SHA256, read with nofollow/nonblock and stable before/open/after/lstat identities.
Gzip expansion is bounded at1MiB; tar is only read into memory. Each member must be a fixed unique plain file, no link or absolute/traversal name; twelve names and136003 total member bytes are exact.
All eleven source-sealed payload members are byte-identical to the separately reviewed actual sealed CI package; the twelfth is its pinned deployment manifest.
All member hashes, fixed destination absence and no-existing-CI result namespaces are checked before any write.

An O_EXCL installation-started claim prevents duplicate installer ownership. New tool directories and twelve fixed payload files use create-only writes, file fsync and exact readback; final directory fsync and a new installation receipt complete the path.
Failure leaves original archive, native installer output and all partial files in place. No in-place replay, overwrite or cleanup is performed.
The only destinations are new exact-CI tools, separate prerequisite module, Q-only foundation and deployment metadata. Existing source, qualification results and cache are not modified.
No compiler, qualifier, CI runner, remote request or benchmark is launched by the installer.
limitations: Static checks do not certify future installation or CI success. Root retains original actual native start/status/read receipts.
Memory tar reads do not execute any included program or create extracted member files.
